Ability to communicate and interact professionally and courteously both orally and in writing with all levels of employees, management and customers
Reliable attendance and punctuality. Anduril is an “in-person” office

Benefits

Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. This role turns complex program requirements into standardized processes, clearly defined work products, repeatable governance, and practical digital tools that improve execution across contracts, engineering, manufacturing, sustainment, finance, and customer engagement.

The role is also responsible for identifying and implementing automation and AI-enabled solutions that reduce manual effort, improve data quality, accelerate analysis, strengthen decision support, and enable more effective product-development and program-execution practices.

Core responsibilities include standardizing program-management processes; integrating contract deliverables and Integrated Master Schedules (IMS); leading cost-account structure creation and maintenance; developing analytical studies and AI-enabled decision-support products; and ensuring that approved methods and tools are embedded into daily execution. The Program Manager also provides direct supervisory leadership to 2–3 Assistant Program Managers, setting priorities, developing team capability, and maintaining consistent execution across assigned resources.

What You'll Do

Portfolio Integration and Baseline Management

Serve as the integration lead across ISV contracts, variants, work directives, and program-management workstreams.
Maintain a consolidated view of technical, schedule, financial, and contractual baselines, including the relationships and trade-offs among them.
Assess the effect of scope, configuration, schedule, resource, and funding changes on the broader ISV portfolio.
Translate contractual requirements into executable plans in partnership with Contracts, Finance, Engineering, Manufacturing, Integrated Product Support, Quality, Supply Chain, and Business Development.
Identify cross-functional dependencies, constraints, and decision points early enough to protect program commitments.

Process Excellence, Work-Product Standardization, and Governance

Define, document, standardize, and maintain end-to-end operating processes for core ISV program-management activities, including contract-change flow, CDRL development and review, IMS updates, risk and issue management, cost-account setup, decision forums, and customer reviews.
Own the development and lifecycle management of reusable work products, including SOPs, process maps, RACI charts, templates, checklists, dashboards, decision briefs, study charters, reporting packs, and training materials.
Establish clear quality standards, entry and exit criteria, ownership models, version control, and approval paths for critical ISV work products.
Convert lessons learned and recurring execution issues into improved standards, updated tools, and practical guidance that teams can apply consistently.
Monitor adoption, compliance, cycle time, quality, and rework; identify gaps and bottlenecks; and lead corrective actions through closure.
Establish a sustainable governance cadence to review, approve, communicate, and continuously improve processes and work products as contracts, tools, organizational responsibilities, and customer expectations evolve.

Automation, AI Enablement, and Product Development

Systematically identify high-friction, manual, repetitive, data-intensive, or error-prone activities in ISV program execution and product-development workflows.
Evaluate opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, or augment work using SharePoint, Power Platform, dashboards, templates, macros, scripts, workflow tools, generative AI, machine learning, and other appropriate technologies.
Lead the development and implementation of AI-based product-development and program-execution solutions, such as requirements analysis, knowledge retrieval, engineering-content comparison, trade-study support, schedule and risk analysis, configuration-change impact assessment, predictive insights, and automated reporting.
Define use cases, data requirements, controls, human-in-the-loop reviews, test cases, acceptance criteria, and responsible-use practices for automation and AI solutions.
Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, IPS, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, IT, data teams, and tool owners to prototype, validate, deploy, and sustain solutions.
Translate user needs into practical product requirements, workflow designs, minimum viable products, adoption plans, training materials, and support processes.
Establish baseline and post-implementation measures for cycle time, error rate, touch time, quality, adoption, decision speed, and realized benefits.
Build a prioritized automation and AI opportunity backlog, manage delivery roadmaps, and ensure solutions become standardized work rather than isolated pilots.

Cost-Account Structure and Financial Integration

Lead the creation and maintenance of cost-account structures for ISV integration activities in close collaboration with Program Finance, Controllership, and Contracts.
Facilitate working sessions to structure new work in accordance with MIL-STD-881 and applicable internal GPN/WBS standards.
Ensure traceability among contract scope, work breakdown structures, cost accounts, charging structures, authorized personnel, and reporting requirements.
Prepare and submit GPN/WBS requests, track approvals, resolve issues, and maintain current reference tools such as ISV GPN guides, PEG/WBS masters, and project lists.
Coordinate with Finance to ensure structures support accurate reporting, invoicing, forecasting, cost control, and audit readiness.
Identify and correct misalignment between authorized work, charge lines, organizational ownership, and program baselines.

Contract Deliverables, CDRLs, and Integrated Master Schedules

Own the contract-deliverables integration plan and ensure CDRLs, technical products, and program artifacts are connected to the appropriate IMS tasks.
Confirm that deliverables are properly scoped, resourced, sequenced, reviewed, and aligned to customer and internal milestones.
Oversee CDRL development, internal review, approval, status tracking, and submission while improving visibility through workflow automation where practical.
Establish performance reporting for deliverables, including on-time, late, at-risk, aging, and recovery-plan status.
Partner with the IMS lead to maintain a high-quality, resource-informed schedule that reflects current scope, approved changes, dependencies, risks, and constraints.
Lead recurring reviews of IMS and deliverable health, elevate conflicts and decision points, and drive closure of recovery actions.

People Leadership and Team Development

Provide day-to-day supervision, work prioritization, coaching, and performance support for 2–3 Assistant Program Managers.
Establish clear assignments, ownership, priorities, and escalation paths across ISV integration activities.
Build team capability in structured program management, data-driven decision support, process discipline, and customer-facing communication.
Ensure effective coverage of portfolio priorities and consistent execution of program-management standards.

Studies and Decision Support

Plan and execute trade studies and analytical projects that inform future engineering content, production strategies, sustainment concepts, business cases, and investment decisions for the ISV vehicle family.
Develop study charters that define the problem statement, objectives, scope, assumptions, alternatives, evaluation criteria, stakeholders, and timeline.
Coordinate analyses across Engineering, Manufacturing, Integrated Product Support, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, Contracts, and Business Development.
Develop data-backed recommendations, scenario comparisons, cost and schedule impacts, and sensitivity analyses for internal leadership reviews and customer engagements.
Translate decisions into accountable actions and ensure resulting changes are incorporated into contracts, baselines, schedules, budgets, and execution plans.

Stakeholder Communication, Risk, and Change Management

Serve as a primary integration point for ISV leadership and provide concise, structured updates on process health, automation progress, IMS status, deliverables, financial structures, and active studies.
Facilitate recurring risk, issue, and opportunity reviews; ensure items are documented, assessed, assigned, mitigated, and linked to affected scope, schedule, cost, and deliverables.

Project Manager | Te Au Reka Programme

Secondment/Fixed Term (3 Years), Full Time

Wellington CBD

Te Au Reka - Improving access to justice for all New Zealanders

Te Au Reka represents the opportunity of a lifetime, making a profound difference to those who work in and interact with our courts and tribunals. We are seeking to modernise the administration of justice by replacing highly manual, time-consuming, paper-based process with a new digital case management solution, transforming the way people access and experience justice in Aotearoa New Zealand.

Te Au Reka is a large, complex and unique programme spanning the courts and tribunals of New Zealand. In delivering Te Au Reka we are seeking to build the Ministry's capability to deliver complex programmes of change. Working on Te Au Reka will give you the opportunity to use your knowledge and experience, while developing new ways of working. We are building a team that is highly collaborative, inquisitive and adaptable. Te Au Reka is a game-changer, and we care deeply about making it a success.

Te Haeata/The Opportunity

We are looking for an experienced and delivery-focused Project Manager
to join the Te Au Reka Programme. In this role, you will lead the planning, delivery, monitoring, and reporting of key projects that support one of New Zealand's most significant justice transformation programmes.

You will work closely with programme teams, subject matter experts, and senior leaders to ensure projects are successfully delivered, risks are proactively managed, and stakeholders remain informed and engaged. You'll play a critical role in aligning project delivery with programme objectives, providing high-quality information to support decision-making, and driving continuous improvement in project and programme practices.

This is an exciting opportunity for a proactive and adaptable project professional who enjoys working in a complex environment, building strong relationships, solving challenging problems, and delivering outcomes that make a meaningful difference. The role requires strong project management expertise, analytical thinking, and the ability to influence and engage stakeholders at all levels of the organisation.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead the planning, execution, monitoring, and delivery of projects within the Te Au Reka programme.
Manage project scope, timelines, risks, issues, dependencies, and resources.
Provide accurate and timely reporting to support leadership and governance decision-making.
Facilitate workshops and stakeholder discussions to drive project outcomes.
Build strong relationships across the Ministry, judiciary, government agencies, suppliers, and programme teams.
Support change management activities to ensure successful implementation of project outcomes.
Contribute to continuous improvement and strengthen programme delivery practices.
Contributing to governance forums and providing insights on implementation risks and delivery status.
Championing high-quality delivery, continuous improvement and collaborative ways of working.

We're looking for someone who combines strong project delivery expertise with excellent stakeholder management skills and a passion for driving successful outcomes.

Relevant tertiary qualification or equivalent professional experience in project management.
Experience delivering complex projects from initiation through to implementation, including planning, scheduling, resource management, risk management, and reporting.
Strong knowledge of project and change management methodologies, including Agile, Waterfall, and/or Prosci.
Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, meet competing deadlines, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organisational skills with strong attention to detail.
Demonstrated experience building and maintaining effective relationships with stakeholders at all levels.
Strong communication skills, including preparing reports, facilitating workshops, and presenting to diverse audiences.
Experience identifying risks and issues, developing practical solutions, and driving successful resolution.
Ability to influence and promote effective project and programme management practices across teams.
High level of proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and project management tools.
Strong collaboration skills and the ability to adapt quickly to changing priorities and complex environments.

Desirable Experience

Experience managing complex programmes or projects within large organisations.
Understanding of public sector environments, governance requirements, and performance reporting.

new_jobs.description:
Location:
This role will be hybrid based out of Ontario and will involve travel to our locations and client sites.

Lifemark Health Group (LHG) is a market leader in customized healthcare solutions. With over 20 years of service excellence, LHG is one of the largest, most trusted, and most comprehensive providers in Canada. As a national healthcare company, LHG employs over 5,000 highly trained clinicians, medical experts and team members in almost 400 locations coast-to-coast and continues to grow both organically as well as through acquisitions. With that growth, is a vision to be the most innovative healthcare providers in community rehabilitation, workplace health and wellness and medical assessment services. Lifemark was acquired by Loblaw Companies on May 10, 2022.

The Opportunity:

The Program Manager is accountable for the end-to-end delivery of Lifemark’s centralized operating model supporting the WSIB programs.

Reporting into the Senior Director, Channel Operations this role serves as the primary point of contact for WSIB, and the Ontario Workers’ Network, and is responsible for overseeing intake, triage, provider network performance, reporting, billing integrity, and service quality across a province-wide network of Lifemark clinics.

The successful candidate will lead a centralized coordination function that ensures injured workers are triaged, treated, and supported through return-to-work in a timely, consistent, and high-quality manner, aligned to defined service level expectations.

Programs you'll be accountable for:
WSIB Specialized Care Program/Ontario Workers’ Network (OWN); WSIB Interdisciplinary Treatment Program of Care; WSIB Musculoskeletal Program of Care; WSIB Mild Traumatic Brain Injury Program of Care; Mental Health Program of Care

Key Responsibilities:

Client Leadership & Governance

Act as the primary interface with the WSIB & OWN for all operational matters
Lead regular governance activities including operational updates, Monthly and Quarterly Business Reviews
Provide proactive communication on program performance, risks, and system pressures
Manage issue escalation and resolution in collaboration with the client

Central Coordination Services (CCS) Operations

Oversee centralized intake, triage, and referral allocation across the province
Ensure workers are matched to appropriate providers based on clinical need, location, and capacity
Monitor and ensure adherence to service level agreements (SLAs), including clinical standards, access, reporting and turnaround times
Coordinate scheduling, rescheduling, and no-show management through centralized processes
Ensure seamless coordination across Lifemark clinics
Oversee onboarding, credentialing, and ongoing program management within clinics
Identify gaps in geographic or service coverage and implement mitigation strategies
Act as escalation point for provider performance issues and conflict resolution

Quality Assurance & Clinical Alignment

Ensure consistent application of quality assurance processes across all providers
Monitor adherence to clinical pathways, documentation standards, and reporting requirements
Partner with clinical leadership to address quality gaps and identify training needs
Drive consistency in service delivery across a multi-provider network

Data, Reporting & Business Intelligence

Oversee development and delivery of program reporting and performance dashboards
Monitor key performance indicators including return-to-work outcomes, service timelines, and provider performance
Analyze trends and translate data into actionable insights and recommendations
Ensure standardized data collection and reporting processes across all providers
Sharing and socializing data insights that inform clinics and leadership on status of the program

Financial Oversight (Billing & Block Model Integrity)

Oversee centralized invoicing and billing processes across all providers
Ensure accuracy and compliance with WSIB block funding requirements
Monitor financial trends, variances, and potential risks
Partner with internal finance teams to support audits, reconciliation, and reporting

Issue Resolution & Continuous Improvement

Act as the central escalation point for operational, clinical, and system-related issues
Lead root cause analysis and implement corrective actions
Identify opportunities to improve workflows, efficiency, and service delivery
Drive continuous improvement across the program based on performance insights

What we're looking for:

7–10+ years of experience in program management, healthcare operations, or large-scale service delivery
Experience managing multi-site or network-based service delivery models
Demonstrated experience with centralized operations, intake models, or care coordination systems
Proven ability to manage complex client relationships, preferably within insurance, WCB/WSIB, or public sector environments
Strong financial and operational acumen, including experience with reporting, billing, and performance management
Experience in rehabilitation, occupational health, or disability management is considered an asset

Core Competencies

Strong systems thinking and operational mindset
High level of ownership and accountability
Data-driven decision making and analytical capability
Ability to manage complexity and perform under pressure
Effective stakeholder management and communication skills

What Success Looks Like

Referrals are triaged and assigned efficiently across the network with minimal delays
Service level agreements are consistently met across all providers
The client has clear, timely, and actionable visibility into program performance
Billing processes are accurate, compliant, and transparent
Treatment clinics are aligned, high-performing, and accountable
Issues are identified and resolved proactively

Inclusion

We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where people from all backgrounds can thrive. Improving inclusion and equity is a collective responsibility. Lifemark promotes equal employment opportunities for all job applicants, including but not limited to those self-identifying as a member of the employment equity groups: Indigenous peoples, Newcomers to Canada, Women, and Visible minorities.

Intermediate analytical modeling skills (e.g. Google Sheets and Excel), and proficiency leveraging SQL to regularly write queries independently

Exceptional communication skills (written and verbal), with a demonstrated ability to tailor messaging for audiences of diverse specializations and high seniority

Proven 0-to-1 execution experience, with a track record of successfully launching new business lines, products, or major strategic initiatives from concept to rollout

new_jobs.title: Stratège, Produits IA | AI Product Strategist
new_jobs.description:
Stratège, Produits IA

Parce que travailler chez Cossette, c'est se brancher sur une énergie créative incomparable. C'est collaborer avec des client·e·s qui flashent sur des projets stimulants qui mettent nos forces en lumière et qui rayonnent mondialement. C'est être entouré·e de gens intelligents et allumés qui ont le feu sacré bien vivant. C'est donner un élan à sa croissance, et sentir qu'on te fait vraiment confiance. Bref, travailler chez Cossette, c'est sentir qu'on passe à un autre niveau.

Ce que tu feras

Nous recherchons un·e stratège en produits IA qui sait autant écouter un client que livrer un produit. Tu comprends les vrais enjeux derrière les besoins exprimés, tu les traduis en vision claire, et tu te mets les mains dans le produit pour que ça se concrétise. Tu es la courroie de transmission entre le client, les designers et les développeurs : tu gardes tout le monde aligné sur ce qui crée de la valeur, tu tranches sur les décisions produit, et tu t'assures que ce qu'on livre a un impact réel pour les utilisateurs finaux.

Le rôle inclut :

Agir comme expert produit IA côté client : animer les rencontres régulières, présenter les fonctionnalités et les évolutions, recueillir les retours et maintenir la relation de confiance tout au long du projet.
Définir et maintenir la vision produit, établir les priorités et assurer que l'équipe reste alignée sur ce qui apporte la plus grande valeur client et utilisateur.
Créer et prioriser le backlog fonctionnel, rédiger les spécifications (spec-driven development), et participer au backlog refinement avec les équipes de développement.
Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les développeur·euses GenAI pour questionner les fonctionnalités, évaluer la faisabilité, estimer les efforts et trancher sur les décisions techniques qui ont un impact produit.
Co-construire la direction produit avec les designers UX/UI : définir ce qui est un oui, ce qui est un non, aligner les priorités et s'assurer que ce qui est planifié est réaliste et livrable.
Piloter la démarche de recherche et de discovery : entrevues utilisateurs, analyse comparative, ateliers de co-création et design thinking, pour ancrer chaque décision dans des insights concrets.
Concevoir et animer des workshops clients et internes pour faire émerger les besoins, aligner les parties prenantes et faire avancer les projets.
Comprendre et cartographier la donnée disponible chez les clients, identifier comment la transformer, l'enrichir ou l'exploiter dans l'architecture du produit IA.
Identifier et prioriser les cas d'usage IA pertinents, qu'il s'agisse de produits B2C, B2B, d'outils internes ou de transformation des façons de travailler d'une organisation.
Assurer le suivi post-déploiement, mesurer la valeur livrée et proposer des optimisations continues.
Maintenir une veille active sur l'écosystème IA générative pour nourrir la vision produit et identifier de nouvelles opportunités pour les clients.

Ce que tu apportes

Un instinct de stratège terrain : tu définis les priorités, tu arbitres, et tu gardes l'équipe alignée sur ce qui compte vraiment.
Une capacité à entendre ce que le client dit, et surtout ce qu'il ne dit pas, pour en faire une direction produit claire et actionnable.
Un vrai mindset de problem solving : devant un obstacle, tu ne t'arrêtes pas, tu cherches la solution et tu fais avancer.
Une aisance en co-création et dans les méthodes de design thinking : entrevues, recherche, analyse comparative, animation de workshops.
Une capacité à travailler en temps réel avec des designers UX/UI et des développeurs, à challenger les approches, à évaluer la faisabilité et à prendre des décisions éclairées.
Une sensibilité à la donnée : tu sais identifier ce qui existe, comprendre comment la transformer et en faire un levier pour les produits que tu construis.
Une capacité à lire et comprendre l'architecture d'un système, à en identifier les forces et les limites, et à proposer des optimisations concrètes en fonction des objectifs produit.
Une compréhension solide de l'écosystème IA générative, des workflows agentiques et de leur potentiel applicatif dans des contextes clients variés.
Un esprit collaboratif et intrapreneurial : tu prends les devants, tu fédères, tu livres.
Capacité à gérer plusieurs mandats en parallèle avec des délais rapides et changeants.

Atouts :

Connaissance des pratiques agiles et des outils de gestion de backlog (Jira, Linear, Notion, etc.).
Familiarité avec les outils d'analytique et de données (GA4, Mixpanel, Looker, Segment, etc.).
Expérience avec des outils de design et de prototypage (Figma, etc.).
Expérience en transformation organisationnelle ou en réinvention de processus internes par l'IA.

Expérience :
5-7 ans en stratégie numérique, gestion de produit ou équivalent, dont au moins 2 ans dans un contexte IA.

Qu'est-ce que tu y gagnes ?

On valorise ta personnalité

Un environnement de travail innovant et entrepreneurial qui encourage l'ingéniosité et l'individualité - avec les meilleurs collègues et les meilleurs clients.
Des modèles de travail hybrides et des horaires flexibles, ainsi qu'une politique de travail de n'importe où pour les séjours de courte durée dans d'autres régions.
Vacances généreuses à partir de 3 semaines + 1 semaine supplémentaire pendant les fêtes de fin d'année.
Des espaces de travail modernes et ouverts, avec des cafés et des snacks, situés au cœur de la ville, à proximité de magasins et de restaurants et avec un accès facile aux transports en commun.
Événements sociaux pour l'équipe - fêtes de fin d'année, rencontres saisonnières, happy hours hebdomadaires, conférences inspirantes et bien plus encore!

On est soucieux de l'apprentissage et de l'amélioration de l'être humain

Sessions d'apprentissage et de développement en interne et conversations annuelles sur la carrière et la croissance
Accès à un réseau interne d'opportunités professionnelles dans toutes les agences du réseau Plus Compagnie
Comités EDI et groupes de ressources employé·es, programmes et initiatives dans l'ensemble de Plus Companie

Découvrez notre rapport EDI ici pour en savoir plus sur notre travail et notre engagement envers l'équité.

On investi dans ta santé et ton bien-être

Des avantages sociaux flexibles pour répondre à ton style de vie et aux étapes de ta vie - avec un accès à un compte personnel que tu peux utiliser pour une grande variété de dépenses, incluant l'abonnement à un centre de conditionnement physique, des soins pour les animaux, des frais d’études et bien d’autres.
Un soutien complet en matière de santé mentale, y compris l’accès à une clinique virtuelle qui t’offre des programmes guidés et personnalisés de thérapie cognitivo-comportementale ainsi que des séances de thérapie en direct, un accès à des cliniciens de la santé 24 heures sur 24, 7 jours sur 7, et un éventail holistique de ressources en matière de santé et de bien-être pour vous et votre famille.
Des salles de santé et de bien-être lorsque tu as besoin d'un endroit pour te ressourcer.
Une politique de congés maladie et personnels responsable conçue afin que tu n'aies pas à t’inquiéter au moment où une obligation ou une urgence survient.
Régime complémentaire de maternité.

Les besoins linguistiques pour le poste sont évalués conjointement entre le gestionnaire et l'équipe d'acquisition de talents.

Ce que tu dois savoir

On est très reconnaissant·e·s par le nombre de personnes talentueuses qui postulent chaque jour pour travailler avec nous. Et on remercie chacun d'entre vous. On contactera directement les personnes que l’on souhaite rencontrer dans le cadre d'un entretien.

Pour garantir une évaluation juste et cohérente de tous les candidats, nos intervieweurs sont assistés d'un outil d'IA qui prend des notes en toute sécurité pendant la conversation.

Pour donner un sens au travail, il faut tenir compte des différents points de vue. On est un employeur qui souscrit au principe de l'égalité des chances et nous ne faisons aucune discrimination fondée sur l'âge, la couleur, les capacités, l'origine nationale, la race, la religion, le sexe ou l'orientation sexuelle. Non seulement ces dispositions sont-elles protégées par les lois provinciales et fédérales, mais l'acceptation de la différence est ce qui fait de Cossette ce qu'elle est, et on ne voudrait pas qu'il en soit autrement. On est fier·ères·s de notre milieu de travail inclusif et accessible. Si vous avez besoin de mesures d'adaptation au cours du processus d'entrevue, faites-le nous savoir.

En rejoignant Cossette, tu fais partie de Plus Compagnie. Ce réseau d'agences entrepreneuriales est fondé sur la collaboration, pas la compétition. Il permet à chaque agence - et à chaque individu - de mettre en commun ses capacités uniques pour créer de la magie. Vous aurez la possibilité de prendre des risques, de rêver en grand, de développer vos compétences et d'évoluer dans votre carrière avec le soutien total du réseau et de tout ce qu'il a à offrir.

EN

Working at Cossette means connecting to an incomparable creative energy. It means collaborating with clients who are excited about stimulating projects that highlight our strengths and resonate globally. It means being surrounded by intelligent and enlightened people who have a vibrant sacred fire. It means boosting your growth, and feeling truly trusted. In short, working at Cossette means feeling like you're moving to the next level.

What You Will Do

We are looking for an AI Product Strategist who knows how to listen to a client as much as they know how to deliver a product. You understand the real issues behind the expressed needs, translate them into a clear vision, and get your hands into the product to make it happen. You are the transmission belt between the client, designers, and developers: you keep everyone aligned on what creates value, you make product decisions, and you ensure that what we deliver has a real impact on the end-users.

The role includes:

Defining and maintaining the product vision, establishing priorities, and ensuring the team remains aligned on what brings the greatest client and user value.
Creating and prioritizing the functional backlog, writing specifications (spec-driven development), and participating in backlog refinement with development teams.
Working closely with GenAI developers to question features, evaluate feasibility, estimate efforts, and make technical decisions that have a product impact.
Co-building the product direction with UX/UI designers: defining what is a yes, what is a no, aligning priorities, and ensuring what is planned is realistic and deliverable.
Leading the research and discovery process: user interviews, comparative analysis, co-creation workshops, and design thinking, to anchor every decision in concrete insights.
Designing and leading client and internal workshops to elicit needs, align stakeholders, and move projects forward.
Understanding and mapping the data available at clients, identifying how to transform, enrich, or exploit it within the AI product architecture.
Identifying and prioritizing relevant AI use cases, whether B2C, B2B products, internal tools, or the transformation of an organization's ways of working.
Ensuring post-deployment follow-up, measuring the value delivered, and proposing continuous optimizations.
Maintaining an active watch on the generative AI ecosystem to inform the product vision and identify new opportunities for clients.

What You Bring

An on-the-ground strategist's instinct: you define priorities, arbitrate, and keep the team aligned on what truly matters.
5-7 years in digital strategy, product management, or equivalent, including at least 2 years in an AI context.
An ability to hear what the client says, and especially what they don't say, to turn it

new_jobs.title: Senior Commercial Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Senior Commercial Operations Analyst

The Senior Commercial Operations Analyst serves as a strategic business partner within the Commercial Operations organization, supporting the design and execution of sales strategies that drive revenue growth, field effectiveness, and organizational performance. Working cross-functionally with Sales Leadership, Marketing, Finance, Operations, and Executive Leadership, this individual provides strategic and analytical support across sales compensation design, sales target and quota setting, commercial planning, territory strategy, executive and board reporting, sales operations, and marketing effectiveness.

Critical Competencies

Commercial & Strategic Acumen:
Understands how sales strategy, compensation, targets, territory design, marketing activity, resource allocation, and operational decisions influence commercial performance. Connects analysis to broader business objectives and practical recommendations.
Analytical Thinking & Decision Support:
Evaluates business performance, identifies meaningful trends and root causes, tests assumptions, and develops actionable recommendations. Uses data as a tool to support decisions rather than treating reporting as the end product.
Executive Communication & Storytelling:
Translates complex commercial information into clear, concise narratives for operational leaders, executives, and board audiences. Communicates not only what the data shows, but why it matters and what actions should follow.
Cross-Functional Partnership:
Builds productive relationships across Sales, Marketing, Finance, Operations, and Executive Leadership to align priorities, solve business problems, and advance commercial initiatives.
Business Planning & Problem Solving:
Approaches ambiguous commercial challenges with curiosity, sound judgment, and a solution-oriented mindset. Balances quantitative analysis with business context when developing recommendations.
Quality, Ownership & Execution:
Maintains strong attention to detail while managing multiple strategic and recurring priorities. Produces accurate, timely work and takes ownership from initial analysis through recommendation and follow-through.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Sales Compensation & Incentive Strategy
Support the design, modeling, evaluation, and ongoing optimization of sales compensation and incentive plans.
Develop scenario models to evaluate plan mechanics, payout curves, thresholds, accelerators, and potential financial and behavioral impacts.
Analyze compensation effectiveness, productivity, attainment, and payout trends to identify opportunities for improvement.
Partner with Sales Leadership and Finance to ensure compensation plans align with commercial objectives, financial expectations, and desired field behaviors.
Support commission reporting, plan communication, and recommendations for future compensation plan changes.

Sales Targets, Quotas & Commercial Planning
Support annual and quarterly sales target and quota-setting processes across territories, regions, and sales teams.
Analyze historical performance, market opportunity, growth expectations, and organizational priorities to inform target recommendations.
Develop territory opportunity assessments and commercial growth analyses to support business planning.
Assist leadership with resource allocation, market prioritization, and performance expectation decisions.
Monitor performance against targets and business plans and recommend corrective actions or adjustments when appropriate.

Commercial Strategy & Business Partnership
Partner with Sales, Marketing, Finance, Operations, and Executive Leadership to evaluate commercial performance and identify growth opportunities.
Conduct ad hoc business analyses that help leadership understand performance drivers, risks, tradeoffs, and strategic options.
Develop recommendations that connect commercial data to business actions rather than relying solely on historical reporting.
Support strategic initiatives, operating reviews, and cross-functional projects impacting sales effectiveness and revenue growth.
Evaluate the potential commercial impact of organizational, market, process, or strategy changes.

Executive & Board Reporting
Develop executive and board-level reporting packages that clearly communicate commercial performance, trends, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Prepare recurring commercial performance reviews, quarterly business reviews, and strategic planning materials.
Build clear narratives around performance results, connecting key metrics to business context and organizational priorities.
Partner with leadership to identify the most meaningful measures and insights for executive decision-making.
Present findings and recommendations in a concise, business-oriented manner appropriate for senior leadership audiences.

Sales Operations & Territory Strategy
Support territory alignment, territory optimization, and field coverage initiatives.
Evaluate geographic coverage, referral density, provider concentration, market opportunity, and field productivity.
Conduct white-space, target account, dormant account, and market opportunity analyses.
Support territory realignment recommendations and monitor performance following organizational or structural changes.
Identify opportunities to improve sales processes, field effectiveness, resource deployment, and commercial operating rhythms.

Marketing & Commercial Effectiveness
Partner with Marketing and Sales Leadership to evaluate targeting strategies, referral generation, campaign effectiveness, provider opportunity, and market penetration.
Analyze the effectiveness of commercial initiatives and recommend changes to improve reach, conversion, productivity, or return on investment.
Support alignment between sales targeting, marketing strategy, and field execution.
Use AcuityMD and other commercial intelligence platforms to identify provider, account, and market opportunities.
Monitor adoption and effectiveness of commercial tools and initiatives and recommend improvements.

Analytics, Forecasting & Decision Support
Perform quantitative and qualitative analyses necessary to support compensation, target setting, territory strategy, forecasting, and commercial planning.
Support monthly, quarterly, and annual forecasting activities and evaluate forecast accuracy.
Analyze performance trends, productivity indicators, referral activity, order volume, and other commercial metrics to identify meaningful business insights.
Maintain accurate recurring reports, scorecards, and analytical tools needed to support commercial decision-making.
Partner with technical and data resources as needed to improve reporting capabilities, data quality, and access to commercial information.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Required
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Marketing, Analytics, or a related field.
Minimum of 3-5 years of experience in Commercial Operations, Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Strategy, Commercial Finance, Sales Compensation, or a related role supporting a complex sales organization.
Demonstrated experience supporting one or more of the following: sales compensation, quota or target setting, commercial planning, territory strategy, executive reporting, or sales performance management.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and the ability to build and interpret financial, compensation, performance, and scenario models.
Strong business acumen with the ability to connect data and analysis to commercial strategy and operational recommendations.
Experience preparing materials, analyses, or presentations for senior leadership or executive audiences.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to simplify complex information and develop clear business narratives.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and collaborate effectively across functions.

Preferred
Experience supporting healthcare, medical device, DME, pharmaceutical, or B2B field sales organizations.
Experience with sales compensation plan design, modeling, or administration.
Experience with territory planning, quota setting, forecasting, or commercial business planning.
Experience partnering with Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Operations in a commercial environment.
Experience developing executive or board-level reporting and presentation materials.
Experience working with Salesforce, AcuityMD, or similar CRM and commercial intelligence platforms.
Working knowledge of Power BI, Tableau, or similar business intelligence tools.
SQL or other advanced data-query experience is a plus but not required.
Master's Degree preferred but not required.

About The Company

Boston Government Services, LLC. (BGS) is a leading engineering, technology, and security firm dedicated to supporting missions of national importance across government programs, national laboratories, security facilities, nuclear operations, and complex commercial projects. With a focus on delivering mission-driven solutions, BGS provides comprehensive services spanning strategic planning, program management, project execution, procurement, supply chain management, quality assurance, safety, security, nuclear, and systems engineering activities. The company prides itself on its extensive experience in secure, highly regulated environments, leveraging expertise to ensure successful delivery and operational excellence for its clients. BGS fosters a culture of openness, inclusivity, and respect, valuing the whole self of its employees. The organization is committed to employee well-being through a comprehensive benefits package and a work environment that emphasizes excellence, collaboration, and professional growth.

About The Role

The Cyber Security Analyst position at BGS is a critical role supporting our clients' cybersecurity operations. The successful candidate will be responsible for monitoring, analyzing, and responding to security incidents, vulnerabilities, and threats within complex environments. This role involves working closely with service owners, IT teams, and security personnel to ensure the integrity and security of client systems. The analyst will perform tasks such as resetting user passwords, analyzing usage patterns, reviewing access requests, triaging unusual activity, and evaluating endpoint detection and response (EDR) coverage. The position requires a proactive approach to threat detection, incident response, and continuous improvement of security processes. The role offers an opportunity to develop and refine cybersecurity skills, contribute to mission-critical projects, and collaborate within a team dedicated to safeguarding client assets against evolving cyber threats.

Qualifications

1–3 years of experience in a Security Operations Center (SOC), cyber security 'blue team', or related role
Strong understanding of TCP/IP, OSI model, and common network protocols (HTTP, DNS, SMTP)
Fundamental knowledge of Windows, Linux, and macOS operating systems
Experience with Active Directory and Azure AD concepts
Proficiency with at least one SIEM platform and one EDR/XDR solution
Experience with ticketing and case management systems
Ability to craft queries using languages such as regex, JSON, and APIs
Basic scripting skills in Python, PowerShell, or Bash
U.S. citizenship and ability to qualify for an HSPD-12 card for two-factor authentication
Successful completion of drug screening
Relevant security certifications (e.g., Security+, CySA+, SSCP) are a plus

Responsibilities

Reset user passwords for compromised or suspected compromised accounts
Collaborate with service owners to reset service account passwords as needed
Ensure proper authorization for in-scope accounts and review access requests
Analyze account usage patterns to identify inactive or inappropriate activity
Review and evaluate approval requests for new access or accounts
Triaging and investigating unusual access requests, such as third-party VPN access or suspicious activity
Assess endpoint security status, including EDR installation and coverage, and coordinate remediation efforts
Monitor external attack surfaces for unapproved or undocumented systems and vulnerabilities
Review systems with public access to ensure compliance with security requirements, including logging and multifactor authentication
Participate in team meetings to discuss current tasks, improvements, and strategic initiatives
Analyze security data and assist in creating playbooks for incident response and threat mitigation
Execute and refine playbooks to respond to detected threats with minimal supervision
Identify telemetry gaps and recommend improvements for detection and visibility
Conduct proactive threat hunting and develop advanced detection use cases based on threat intelligence
Lead investigations from triage to containment, providing detailed reports on root causes, IOCs, and impacted assets
Coordinate containment and remediation activities, including host isolation, credential resets, and blocking malicious activity

Benefits

Competitive total compensation package
Health, Dental, and Vision insurance coverage
Life Insurance and Disability benefits
Paid Vacation and Holidays
401(k) retirement plan with company matching
Opportunities for professional development and training
A collaborative and inclusive work environment that values diversity and innovation

Equal Opportunity

BGS is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment that respects and values diversity in all its forms.

The Global Trade Compliance team operates across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC regions in close collaboration with Husky’s Legal department. As the Global Trade Compliance Program Manager, you will report to the Director, Global Trade Compliance & Customs and serve as the program lead for enterprise-wide trade compliance initiatives. This role will focus on managing global compliance projects, optimizing processes, and ensuring the successful integration of trade compliance requirements into Husky’s systems.

You will partner with cross-functional teams—including Supply Chain, Engineering, IT, Finance, and Sales—to strengthen Husky’s global trade compliance framework, enhance operational efficiency, and reduce compliance risk across all regions.

Key Responsibilities

Program and Project Management

Lead the planning, execution, and delivery of global trade compliance initiatives, including process optimization, technology integration, and system enhancements.

Manage the implementation of trade compliance modules within the ERP system to ensure alignment with global regulatory requirements.

Establish and maintain project governance, milestones, KPIs, and reporting mechanisms for trade compliance programs.

Coordinate global stakeholders to ensure timely completion of key deliverables and consistent global deployment of compliance practices.

Regulatory Compliance and Oversight

Stay current on international trade laws, import regulations/tariffs, export control regulations, and sanctions programs applicable to Husky’s business activities.

Translate complex regulatory requirements into actionable business processes and internal controls.

Collaborate with Engineering and Legal teams to establish export control measures and export authorization processes globally.

Monitor the effectiveness of trade compliance procedures and implement corrective actions as needed.

Classification, Licensing, and Documentation

Lead efforts to standardize global product classification processes, including export control, HTS, and country-of-origin determinations.

Develop and maintain processes for end-use/end-user certifications, license applications, and transaction due diligence.

Ensure accuracy and consistency in trade data, documentation, and system configurations supporting export and customs compliance.

Risk Management and Continuous Improvement

Conduct global risk assessments and audits to evaluate compliance performance and identify improvement opportunities.

Develop risk mitigation strategies to prevent export control or import customs violations.

Drive continuous improvement initiatives leveraging digital tools and automation to enhance compliance monitoring and reporting.

Support internal investigations and voluntary disclosures, when applicable.

Training, Communication, and Stakeholder Engagement

Develop and deliver global training programs to increase awareness of export control, sanctions, and customs requirements.

Promote a culture of compliance through proactive communication and cross-functional collaboration.

Partner with IT, Supply Chain, and Finance to ensure trade compliance considerations are embedded in business processes.

Provide input in communications with government authorities and external consultants regarding trade compliance projects and inquiries.

Required Experience & Education

10+ years of progressive experience in global trade compliance, covering export controls, customs, sanctions, and trade agreements.

Deep understanding of U.S., EU, and Canadian export control and sanctions laws, with additional experience in UK, Swiss, Chinese, and other jurisdictions considered an asset.

Proven track record in managing large-scale trade compliance or ERP integration projects within a multinational organization.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, International Business, Law, Supply Chain, or related discipline; PMP or other project management certification preferred.

Strong analytical and organizational skills, with the ability to interpret complex regulations and translate them into practical business solutions.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of influencing and engaging stakeholders across multiple levels and functions.

Demonstrated ability to lead change, manage competing priorities, and deliver results under tight deadlines in a global environment.

Rhythm is a renewable energy and technology company headquartered in Houston, Texas. We combine energy market expertise with technology, design, and data science to create products and services that deliver affordable green energy and an exceptional customer experience.

We’re hiring an Operations Analyst to join Rhythm’s Operations team and help deliver the exceptional customer experience that sits at the heart of our business.

Analyze customer feedback and operational data to identify trends, recurring issues, and root causes
Turn those insights into recommendations that improve customer experience and operational efficiency
Document workflows, resolutions, and best practices to strengthen Rhythm’s internal knowledge base and improve team consistency
Collaborate cross-functionally to surface bugs, operational risks, and customer-impacting issues

What You’ll Bring

2+ years of experience in a contact center, customer support, customer operations, or similar customer-facing environment

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to handle escalations and difficult customer situations professionally

Customer escalations and complex account issues are handled with empathy, accuracy, and a strong sense of ownership

Job Summary

NORC at the University of Chicago is seeking a qualified Data Analyst I or II (we are open to hiring at either level) to join the Health Sciences Department to support hospital discharge data processing across states and harmonizing and packaging files into a uniform format. At NORC, Data Analysts are early career team members who train and work with our senior Research Scientists, Statisticians, and Data Scientists to perform tasks such as data processing, quality assurance, analysis, and dissemination.

As part of their data processing responsibilities, Data Analysts import, clean, standardize, transform, and validate data sets. They also research and document data procedures and support the investigation of data problems. They may identify, analyze, and interpret trends or patterns in data sets, and help prepare data presentations and reports, including developing charts, graphs, and tables. In addition, the Data Analyst may assist in data collection and harmonization from primary or secondary data sources (e.g., administrative records, commercial data, social media data), preparing data files for delivery, and the maintenance of databases, data systems, and their relevant metadata/dictionaries. The Data Analyst is expected to work collaboratively in a team environment.

For this role, proficiency in SAS is a requirement. Experience with R or Python is welcome but not essential. Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is preferred, and strong documentation practices are important.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Location : This is a hybrid role based in either our Chicago Loop or downtown DC office, with a minimum of six days per month in the office. Exceptional remote candidates may be considered as well.

DEPARTMENT: Health Science Research

NORC’s Health Sciences staff produce rich data on social priorities including child development and healthy aging, the uses of electronic clinical data in research, and the applications and effectiveness of health information technology.

The Health Sciences team is versatile and experienced in data acquisition, management, technical assistance, and analysis; the use of information technology in health care; and numerous data collection methods. Our track record of leadership and innovation includes the design and management of large-scale surveys, including extensive experience collecting biomeasures.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with researchers, statisticians, data scientists, technology experts, and subject matter experts to implement and improve data management, processing, and analysis activities.
Develop programs and scripts for data cleaning, integration, transformation, and harmonization, as well as data quality checks and validation
Support and enhance applications and databases already built for various research needs and produce data documentation and dictionaries.
Contribute to documentation, reports, and presentations through writing sections, creating basic analytic summaries, and developing tables and graphics.
Apply AI tools to help improve efficiency.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills

Bachelor’s degree in one of the following fields: quantitative social sciences, public health, statistics, biostatistics, health informatics, math, data science, or computer science, or related field required.
Proficiency with data management and data processing.
0-2 years’ experience in positions of increasing responsibility, preferably working with large data sets, and conducting statistical/analytic programming (internships included).
Strong foundation in areas of statistics, mathematics, and data science.
Proficient coding skills in SAS are required, including experience with SAS macros
Additional experience with R or Python is welcome but not essential.
Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is preferred.
Strong skills in problem solving and quantitative analysis are required. Able to organize and prioritize work assignments to meet project needs.
Outstanding interpersonal and critical reasoning skills.
Proficiency with MS Office software.

Please include a Resume and Cover Letter when applying. Candidates should be prepared to provide professional references upon request.

Salary And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $62,000 –
$77,000.

Benefits

This position is classified as regular. Regular staff are eligible for NORC’s comprehensive benefits program. Benefits include, but are not limited to:

Generously subsidized health insurance, effective on the first day of employment
Dental and vision insurance
A defined contribution retirement program, along with a separate voluntary 403(b) retirement program
Group life insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance
Benefits that promote work/life balance, including generous paid time off, holidays; paid parental leave, bereavement leave, tuition assistance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

NORC is committed to equity and transparency in its pay practices. We publish salary ranges and benefit information for every job. The listed hiring range reflects what we, in good faith, expect to pay at the time of posting, though actual compensation may vary and may be adjusted over time. A candidate’s placement within the range depends on factors such as competencies, education, qualifications, experience, skills, performance, and organizational needs.

What We Do

NORC at the University of Chicago is an objective, non-partisan research institution that delivers reliable data and rigorous analysis to guide critical programmatic, business, and policy decisions. Since 1941, our teams have conducted groundbreaking studies, created and applied innovative methods and tools, and advanced principles of scientific integrity and collaboration. Today, government, corporate, and nonprofit clients around the world partner with us to transform increasingly complex information into useful knowledge.

Who We Are

For over 80 years, NORC has evolved in many ways, moving the needle with research methods, technical applications and groundbreaking research findings. But our tradition of excellence, passion for innovation, and commitment to collegiality have remained constant components of who we are as a brand, and who each of us is as a member of the NORC team. With world-class benefits, a business casual environment, and an emphasis on continuous learning, NORC is a place where people join for the stellar research and analysis work for which we’re known, and stay for the relationships they form with their colleagues who take pride in the impact their work is making on a global scale.

Job Summary

NORC at the University of Chicago is seeking a qualified Data Analyst I or II (we are open to hiring at either level) to join the Health Sciences Department to support hospital discharge data processing across states and harmonizing and packaging files into a uniform format. At NORC, Data Analysts are early career team members who train and work with our senior Research Scientists, Statisticians, and Data Scientists to perform tasks such as data processing, quality assurance, analysis, and dissemination.

As part of their data processing responsibilities, Data Analysts import, clean, standardize, transform, and validate data sets. They also research and document data procedures and support the investigation of data problems. They may identify, analyze, and interpret trends or patterns in data sets, and help prepare data presentations and reports, including developing charts, graphs, and tables. In addition, the Data Analyst may assist in data collection and harmonization from primary or secondary data sources (e.g., administrative records, commercial data, social media data), preparing data files for delivery, and the maintenance of databases, data systems, and their relevant metadata/dictionaries. The Data Analyst is expected to work collaboratively in a team environment.

For this role, proficiency in SAS is a requirement. Experience with R or Python is welcome but not essential. Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is preferred, and strong documentation practices are important.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Location : This is a hybrid role based in either our Chicago Loop or downtown DC office, with a minimum of six days per month in the office. Exceptional remote candidates may be considered as well.

DEPARTMENT: Health Science Research

NORC’s Health Sciences staff produce rich data on social priorities including child development and healthy aging, the uses of electronic clinical data in research, and the applications and effectiveness of health information technology.

The Health Sciences team is versatile and experienced in data acquisition, management, technical assistance, and analysis; the use of information technology in health care; and numerous data collection methods. Our track record of leadership and innovation includes the design and management of large-scale surveys, including extensive experience collecting biomeasures.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with researchers, statisticians, data scientists, technology experts, and subject matter experts to implement and improve data management, processing, and analysis activities.
Develop programs and scripts for data cleaning, integration, transformation, and harmonization, as well as data quality checks and validation
Support and enhance applications and databases already built for various research needs and produce data documentation and dictionaries.
Contribute to documentation, reports, and presentations through writing sections, creating basic analytic summaries, and developing tables and graphics.
Apply AI tools to help improve efficiency.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills

Bachelor’s degree in one of the following fields: quantitative social sciences, public health, statistics, biostatistics, health informatics, math, data science, or computer science, or related field required.
Proficiency with data management and data processing.
0-2 years’ experience in positions of increasing responsibility, preferably working with large data sets, and conducting statistical/analytic programming (internships included).
Strong foundation in areas of statistics, mathematics, and data science.
Proficient coding skills in SAS are required, including experience with SAS macros
Additional experience with R or Python is welcome but not essential.
Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is preferred.
Strong skills in problem solving and quantitative analysis are required. Able to organize and prioritize work assignments to meet project needs.
Outstanding interpersonal and critical reasoning skills.
Proficiency with MS Office software.

Please include a Resume and Cover Letter when applying. Candidates should be prepared to provide professional references upon request.

Salary And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $62,000 –
$77,000.

Benefits

This position is classified as regular. Regular staff are eligible for NORC’s comprehensive benefits program. Benefits include, but are not limited to:

Generously subsidized health insurance, effective on the first day of employment
Dental and vision insurance
A defined contribution retirement program, along with a separate voluntary 403(b) retirement program
Group life insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance
Benefits that promote work/life balance, including generous paid time off, holidays; paid parental leave, bereavement leave, tuition assistance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

NORC is committed to equity and transparency in its pay practices. We publish salary ranges and benefit information for every job. The listed hiring range reflects what we, in good faith, expect to pay at the time of posting, though actual compensation may vary and may be adjusted over time. A candidate’s placement within the range depends on factors such as competencies, education, qualifications, experience, skills, performance, and organizational needs.

What We Do

NORC at the University of Chicago is an objective, non-partisan research institution that delivers reliable data and rigorous analysis to guide critical programmatic, business, and policy decisions. Since 1941, our teams have conducted groundbreaking studies, created and applied innovative methods and tools, and advanced principles of scientific integrity and collaboration. Today, government, corporate, and nonprofit clients around the world partner with us to transform increasingly complex information into useful knowledge.

Who We Are

For over 80 years, NORC has evolved in many ways, moving the needle with research methods, technical applications and groundbreaking research findings. But our tradition of excellence, passion for innovation, and commitment to collegiality have remained constant components of who we are as a brand, and who each of us is as a member of the NORC team. With world-class benefits, a business casual environment, and an emphasis on continuous learning, NORC is a place where people join for the stellar research and analysis work for which we’re known, and stay for the relationships they form with their colleagues who take pride in the impact their work is making on a global scale.

NORC is an equal opportunity employer. NORC evaluates qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, sexual orientation, and other legally protected characteristics.

Job Description

We are seeking a Program Manager
to independently lead assigned cross-functional programs within Platform Enablement, bringing disciplined execution and reliable follow-through from planning through delivery. Our team helps Autodesk teams discover, adopt, extend, and contribute to shared platform technology.

You will partner with the Principal Program Manager and broader team to advance cross-functional work, collaborating with product, engineering, operations, and other business partners. You will own the day-to-day planning, dependency and risk management, and stakeholder follow-through for assigned programs or discrete workstreams within broader initiatives. You will resolve day-to-day delivery issues independently, recommend options when tradeoffs arise, and escalate decisions that affect strategy, priorities, multiple programs, or require senior alignment.

This is a program management role with a strong business analysis and data component. You will use process analysis, requirements clarification, metrics, and reporting to improve execution and help teams make better decisions. Success in this role requires accountability, sound judgment, proactive communication, and comfort navigating ambiguity.

At Autodesk, we build tools that help innovators design and make a better world. We offer a flexible, inclusive environment where people can do meaningful work and grow their careers.

Responsibilities

Independently lead the day-to-day execution of assigned cross-functional programs and discrete workstreams, maintaining clear outcomes, plans, milestones, owners, dependencies, risks, actions, and decisions.

Build trusted relationships across technical and non-technical teams, clarify roles and decision paths, and ensure stakeholders have the context and visibility needed to act.
Maintain lightweight roadmaps, trackers, and reliable sources of truth that make progress, ownership, priorities, dependencies, and risks visible.
Manage recurring operating rhythms for planning, review, learning, and continuous improvement, ensuring decisions and actions are documented and carried forward.
Proactively identify risks, gaps, competing priorities, and dependencies; recommend practical actions; and help prevent issues from becoming blockers.
Apply business analysis and data skills to clarify requirements, map processes, identify patterns, and define useful metrics and reporting that improve execution and decision-making.
Use AI tools responsibly to improve program execution, analysis, communication, documentation, and reporting, and identify opportunities to reduce manual effort or improve quality.

Assess program data, measures, processes, and documentation to identify the highest-value gaps and improvement opportunities.

By 60–90 days: create visibility and momentum

Assigned programs have clear outcomes, plans, ownership, dependencies, risks, and consistent follow-through.
Recurring operating meetings run reliably and result in clear decisions, actions, and measurable progress between sessions.

Stakeholders receive timely, relevant communication and have the context and visibility needed to fulfill their commitments.
Routine delivery and stakeholder issues are resolved independently, with appropriate escalation when broader or senior alignment is required.

By 6 months: scale impact

Assigned programs move forward predictably through independent leadership within established priorities and operating standards.
Stakeholders have a reliable experience working with the team because ownership, communication, commitments, and follow-through are clear and consistent.
Program metrics and reporting provide trusted evidence of progress, health, risks, and outcomes for planning and decision-making.
Lightweight, repeatable processes improve consistency, stakeholder experience, and delivery without adding unnecessary bureaucracy.
Lessons from assigned programs contribute to practical improvements in the broader Platform Enablement operating system, including responsible uses of AI and automation.

Demonstrated ability to drive cross-functional work from planning through execution, including managing milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, and follow-through.
Strong program management judgment, ownership, and independence, with the ability to maintain momentum and escalate appropriately.
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to build trust, create alignment, and influence across technical and non-technical teams without direct authority.
Business analysis and systems-thinking skills, including process analysis, requirements clarification, synthesis, and understanding interdependencies and downstream impacts.
Strong analytical and data skills, including experience defining meaningful metrics and creating useful dashboards or reporting from structured data.
Experience using program management and collaboration platforms such as Airtable, along with comfort learning new technical tools and concepts in a software or technology environment.
Practical experience using AI tools responsibly to improve program management, analysis, communication, or operational workflows.

The Supply Chain Project Manager serves as the primary liaison between Menasha Packaging and its customers for order and inventory management along with supply chain–related initiatives. Provide clear, proactive communication to customers and internal stakeholders on order or initiative status, risks, and next steps.
Identify potential issues early and work collaboratively to resolve them.
Escalate risks or misalignment appropriately while proposing practical solutions.

Supply Chain Insight & Support

Assist with post‑run reviews to ensure objectives are met and lessons learned are captured.

Continuous Improvement

Identify opportunities to improve how Menasha manages customer‑driven supply chain initiatives.
Share best practices and lessons learned across the organization.
Help refine communication and coordination processes between customers and internal teams.

Strong coordination, communication, and organizational skills.

Relationship‑oriented and customer‑focused
Strong communicator and facilitator

Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for a full-time Lead Project Manager - Licensed Environmental Professional
to support our environmental operations, in our Shelton and Glastonbury, CT offices
. Be involved in projects with our Earth and Environment Team
and be a part of a growing organization that meets our client’s objectives and solves their challenges.

Role purpose

Lead the technical and operational delivery of medium to large environmental projects. Coordinate multidisciplinary work, maintain quality and regulatory compliance, and serve as a reliable day-to-day client and agency contact.

Your Impact

Essential Accountabilities

Plan and deliver environmental assessments, permitting and remediation-related work, including Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments.
Lead technical review of field data, analyses, impact evaluations, permit applications, reports and recommendations.
Coordinate project teams, budgets, schedules, hours, expenses and task completion; apply QA/QC and health and safety requirements.
Guide junior project members and coordinate effectively with clients, regulators, resource agencies and technical disciplines.
Support project scoping, proposals and business development while keeping current with relevant environmental science and regulatory practices.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Essential Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in environmental science, ecology, natural resource management or a related life sciences field.
8+ years of relevant environmental consulting/science experience, including surveys, fieldwork, impact assessment and/or construction monitoring.
Experience with State and Federal environmental regulations and permitting, Phase I/II ESAs, technical reporting and regulatory documentation.
Strong technical writing, critical thinking, client coordination and ability to lead junior or project team members. Ability to meet project-specific scheduling and occasional travel requirements.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.

WSP Benefits

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on a providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Compensation

Expected Salary (all locations): $120,000 - $150,000

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and offer for this position, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities in addition to internal equity and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.
